rationale: Re-recorded the account for receipt 29f7b510513642f499f8646cb55dccfe (the previous attempt was replaced inside its turn and never accepted, which the state check confirmed): on a five-voter committed configuration the restarted holder acknowledged one commit on a single copy and, once a majority that never held it formed leadership in a higher term and the holder was rebuilt, the payload was absent from every store, so the acknowledged commit was discarded. The earlier three-voter fact is qualified to that shape, the loss is recorded as its own fact, and the question's current account no longer lists the discard as unexercised.

knowledge.statement: In the retained three-voter execution, a commit acknowledged to the client rested on a single copy of the committed configuration: the restarted instance's Apply completed (acknowledged true, payload index 113) while only it held that payload (payload_on_victims 0, durable_copies 1, durable_on_majority false), the two other voters reconstructed their own three-voter configuration and elected new leadership without it, and after the holder rejoined the payload was still present only there (payload_on_holder_after_rejoin true at index 113) with the new leadership formed in the same term as the stale leader (both 3).
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster whose committed configuration entry sits at log index 106 while the restarted instance's snapshot metadata carries a single-voter configuration; every instance is stopped before the restart, the restarted instance is the only running member when it acknowledges the commit, the other two voters are then rebuilt with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled, and the payload is searched for in every store across its first-to-last index. The survival of that single copy is specific to this shape: with five committed voters and a successor leadership in a strictly higher term the same construction ends with the payload absent from every store (receipt 29f7b510513642f499f8646cb55dccfe).
knowledge.changed_premise: The earlier revision left room to read the single-copy acknowledgement as recoverable while the holder existed. The five-voter receipt shows the same divergence ending with the acknowledged payload discarded from every store once a majority that never held it forms higher-term leadership, so the recorded survival is a property of this three-voter shape (successor leadership in the same term), not of the defect in general.

knowledge.statement: In the retained five-voter execution an acknowledged commit was discarded from every store: the restarted holder acknowledged one payload on a single copy of the committed configuration (acknowledged true, reconstructed_config_voters 1 against the five voters recorded at log index 110, holder term 3), the four returning voters elected leadership at term 3 without it, that leader was stopped so the remaining three elected again at term 4, and once the holder was rebuilt the payload was absent from all five stores (copies_after_rejoin 0, payload_on_holder_after false, discarded true, durable_on_majority false); the flag-disabled control could not acknowledge anything at all.
knowledge.conditions: Five-voter cluster whose committed configuration entry sits at log index 110 while the restarted holder's snapshot metadata carries the demoted single-voter configuration (snapshot_config_voters 1); the four returning voters are rebuilt with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled so their configuration comes from their logs; one extra legal election (the first returning leader stopped, the remaining three of five still a quorum) puts the successor leadership in a strictly higher term before the holder rejoins; the payload is searched for in every store across its first-to-last index.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 29f7b510513642f499f8646cb55dccfe (completed, exit 0, TestAssuranceRestoreCommittedLogsContext passed, 39 parsed events) executes the last open consequence and completes the question. On a committed five-voter configuration whose snapshot metadata records one voter (discard_inputs at parsed index 35: log_config_voters 5, snapshot_config_voters 1), the restarted holder reconstructed a single voter, became leader and acknowledged one payload on a single copy; comparison 2 holds at parsed index 38 for the flag-disabled control, which acknowledged nothing ("node is not the leader", reconstructed_config_voters 5). The four returning voters reconstructed the committed five-voter configuration and elected leadership at term 3 without that payload, a second legal election followed at term 4, and after the holder was rebuilt the payload was present in no store: comparison 1 holds at parsed index 36 with discarded true, payload_on_holder_after false and copies_after_rejoin 0, and comparison 0 is violated at the same index because the acknowledged commit was not durable on a majority of the committed configuration [leader_commitment, commitment_impl, quorum_size]. A client whose Apply completed therefore lost that write once a majority that never held it took over, which is precisely the guarantee a committed entry is supposed to carry. The current account, each result under its own receipt, is: NewRaft's configuration scan starts above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied) and restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied to the tracked commit index first, so a committed configuration entry inside that prefix is never re-derived [scan_start, restore_lastapplied, cfg_entry]; the reconstruction then differs from the node's own log in both directions and across four ladders (receipts 63d4401225884bdd9c75fbe580336c63, faa52ef8ac8a422aa26e12582959eda1, c7938884cd87410eb02432e32dc092ce, 29f7b510513642f499f8646cb55dccfe), keeps a snapshot-derived origin where a snapshot exists, and persists under a live healthy leader until a configuration entry is appended (a1c98fc2bafd4775aa05275dd25f2767); the resulting context leaves a sole committed member unable to campaign or contending for a quorum it can never reach, lets a node take leadership and commit with support from a minority of the committed configuration, ends with a client-acknowledged commit either resting on one copy or being discarded entirely, and lets an empty reconstruction grant and durably record a vote for a peer that holds no vote (5cb138c50c7241b6a2e9f6c7a8698550 with @empty_config_vote_gate). The limitation recorded in earlier accounts that the discard was unexercised is withdrawn; the surviving boundaries are listed below.
counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.

Competing explanation that the flag's committed-log replay itself, rather than the skipped configuration entry, produces these effects: excluded wherever tested, by the within-flag case whose configuration entry lies above the replayed prefix and by the flag-disabled controls in every receipt, which hold the published configuration and refuse the same requests and decisions.

The discard required an extra legal election to put the successor leadership in a strictly higher term: with the successor in the same term as the stale holder the acknowledged copy survived on the holder (receipt c7938884cd87410eb02432e32dc092ce, and the first form of this probe), so the loss depends on the successor outranking the stale holder's term rather than on the divergence alone.

In every case the returning voters were rebuilt with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled on purpose, so their own configuration comes from their logs; the exercised question is what one divergent node's context does, not what a cluster of such nodes would do.
limitations: Single process with in-memory transports and in-memory commit-tracking stores, no crash injection, no disk-backed store and no network fault model.

The exercises restart one instance at a time, build membership ladders from demote/promote or remove, and use single-shot windows (200-1200 ms depending on the case, 3000 ms for leadership, 1000-1500 ms for commits); no rate, repetition or long-run stability claim follows.

The vote-path result rests on a request whose campaign decision and term claim are synthesized from a real peer's identity, address and log; pre-vote delivery was not exercised and only shares the same guards by source inspection.
Reconstruction shapes other than the four exercised ladders, other stores and other flags were not varied.
